purpose: Contract for deterministic/cheap primitive mutation. Teleon should mutate simple primitives into variants (batch input, output adapters, graph composition, cheaper model/provider swaps) through deterministic wrappers and contract records before asking an LLM to rewrite source.
variation_record_law: Every primitive variation stores variation_of, variant, mutation_kind, mutation_summary, base_contract, new_contract, proofs, status, created_at, and serves_truth=false.
io_contract_law: Input/output is managed through primitive contracts: input_contract, output_contract, guardrails, dependencies, execution_surface, logs_schema. A graph edge maps one primitive output contract to the next primitive input contract.

supported_mutations_phase1.rule: Wrap a scalar callable with normalize_to_sequence + map_sequence so one-item code accepts scalar_or_sequence input without rewriting business logic.
Wrap a primitive output into a named object field when the next primitive expects an object contract.
Compose ordered primitive contracts as a compact graph plan with maps_output_to_input edges.
Every primitive graph execution emits JSON-serializable logs with graph_id, primitive_id, status, timing fields, output shape, error, and serves_truth=false.

supported_mutations_later.rule: Replace an LLM-backed primitive with a cheaper model or deterministic parser only if guardrail pass rate stays above threshold.
Replace LLM/browser scraping with CSS/XPath/regex/table extraction after observed pages show stable structure.
Swap third-party API primitive with local/self-hosted implementation behind the same input/output contract when customer control requires it.
Add retry, cache, timeout, proxy, rate-limit, or backoff adapters as graph nodes rather than rewriting primitive internals.
Turn sequence processing into bounded parallel batches only after the scalar->sequence contract is proven.

ci_cd_law: A primitive variation may enter a customer repo as source code, package dependency, private service call, or third-party API call, but every form must carry the same contract, proof record, license/dependency metadata, SBOM/provenance hook, and rollback path.
byok_law: Any LLM-backed primitive must support provider/model/key injection by policy (BYOK or platform key), record which model/provider executed, and permit cheaper/local substitutes when guardrails pass.
marketplace_law: Marketplace primitives are allowed for specialized or proactively maintained capabilities, but they are governed as contract-compatible implementations, not opaque truth. Customers must see code/proof metadata for local primitives and dependency/security posture for hosted/API primitives.
control_vs_cost_tradeoff: Lower token burn is not enough for enterprise adoption. Teleon must preserve control, auditability, patch posture, SSO/BYOK/compliance integration, and customer-owned deployment options.
